title: Coleman Frame
oneLine: A welded frame I built so a Coleman cooler could ride in the truck without shifting.

hero.alt: Generated stand-in image for Coleman Frame. Not a photograph of the real build.

intake.question: What is it, in one sentence?
intake.hint: What it is and what it holds. A frame for what, mounted to what.

intake.question: Role, timeline, status
intake.hint: Solo, how long it took, is it on the vehicle now, how many trips it has done.

intake.question: What made it hard?
intake.hint: Load, weight, packaging around the vehicle, welding thin wall, or working without a proper jig.
intake.answer: The frame had to hold a load that shifts under braking and over washboard, in a space that was already spoken for, without ending up heavier than the thing it carries.

intake.question: What did you decide, and what did you reject?
intake.hint: Material and process. Why that tube size and wall thickness. Steel versus aluminum. MIG versus TIG. What you rejected and why.
intake.answer: I built it as a welded frame sized to the object rather than an adjustable rack that would fit anything. Adjustable would have been more useful in theory and would have rattled itself loose in practice.

intake.question: What number can you put on it?
intake.hint: Frame weight, load carried, tube OD and wall, number of welds, cost, miles traveled on it.

intake.question: What broke, and what did you do?
intake.hint: A weld that cracked, a fitment problem, something that worked loose on the highway.

intake.question: What media do you have?
intake.hint: Tacked up in the jig, the finished welds close enough to see the beads, and it loaded in the field. Close-up weld photos are the proof and most people forget to take them.

intake.question: What would you do differently?
intake.hint: Two sentences. Not self criticism, a design judgement you would make differently now.
